answer.rationale: Write-path p99 at 5x starting ~30 minutes after a release is the strongest reversible correlation, and memory_b1 describes a clean prior build. Regional confinement also makes failover (memory_b2) a live alternative, so those two archives should be checked before lock-in. Circuit breaking is rejected: failing fast would drop customer writes and violate the objective. Failover during peak settlement still looks write-lossy if replication or in-flight settlements are involved, so it stays second until verified. Capacity add and read-replica routing do not explain a change-timed write-path regression. Cause is not identified; primary-only symptoms could be settlement affinity rather than a bad build.
